title: Security Appendix Requests Intake & Redline Tracking (Sales/SE → Security/GRC → Legal)
author: Sofia Mendes
content:
## Purpose
This page defines the **intake process** for requests to update or negotiate a customer’s **Security Appendix / Security Exhibit / Information Security Addendum** (collectively: “Security Appendix”), and the **system of record** for tracking redlines and approved language.

This process is designed to:
- Keep commitments consistent across deals and renewal cycles
- Ensure **Security/GRC** and **Legal** approve any customer-facing security commitments
- Provide a repeatable workflow and clear SLAs for Sales and Solutions Engineering (SE)

> Scope note: This page covers **security appendix language updates and redline handling**. It does **not** cover sharing compliance evidence (SOC 2, pen test summaries, etc.). For evidence requests, follow the Security & Compliance SOP: **Customer Security Review Process** (linked above).

---

## When to use this process
Use this intake when any of the following are requested by a prospect/customer:
- Changes to Redwood’s standard Security Appendix language (adds/removes commitments)
- Customer-provided security addendum that needs review and response
- Contractual commitments around: incident notification timelines, audit rights, data retention, data residency, encryption/KMS/HSM, subprocessor obligations, vulnerability remediation SLAs, or logging
- Any request that requires Redwood to warrant or certify specific security controls beyond approved boilerplate

Do **not** use this intake for:
- Routine security questionnaires or RFPs that can be answered using the **Standard RFP Response Library**
- Evidence sharing requests (SOC 2 report, bridge letter, pen test summary) — route to Security/GRC evidence process
- Product feature requests (e.g., “add SCIM”, “add EU region”, “custom audit log events”) — open a Product ticket instead; do not negotiate roadmap commitments in contract language

---

## Quick decision tree (Sales/SE)
1) **Is the customer asking for documents/evidence (SOC 2, pen test, policies)?**
   - Yes → Follow **Customer Security Review Process** (Security/GRC)
   - No → Continue

2) **Is this a questionnaire/RFP and the question matches an approved answer?**
   - Yes → Use **Standard RFP Response Library** and respond
   - No/Unsure → Continue

3) **Is the customer asking to change contractual security terms (Security Appendix)?**
   - Yes → Submit an intake request (below)

---

## Intake channels (single source of truth)
All Security Appendix update requests must be submitted via **Legal Intake** and must include the required context fields.

**Primary intake:**
- Legal Intake form (internal) → routes to **Finance/Legal Contracts Queue**

**If the form is unavailable:**
- Email alias: **legal-intake@redwoodinference.com** (internal) with subject: "Security Appendix Redline – <Customer> – <Opportunity/Deal ID>"

**Do not** submit Security Appendix changes only via Slack.
- Slack can be used for coordination, but the request is not considered “in progress” until it is logged in the Legal queue.

---

## Required information (must be provided)
Include the following in the intake submission. Missing items will delay triage.

1) **Customer + deal context**
- Customer legal name
- Deal type: New / Renewal / Expansion
- Deployment mode(s): Hosted / Dedicated / Private
- Region(s) involved (e.g., US, EU)
- Target close date and timeline constraints

2) **Artifacts**
- Customer’s redlined document (Word preferred) OR marked-up PDF
- Redwood standard Security Appendix version used as baseline (if known)

3) **What changed (summary)**
- Bullet list of requested changes (or paste key clause excerpts)
- Highlight “must-have” vs “nice-to-have” items if customer shared priorities

4) **Business / risk context**
- ARR / commit size (range acceptable)
- Industry/regulatory drivers (e.g., healthcare, financial services)
- Any commitments already discussed verbally (include exact wording used)

5) **Point of contact**
- AE + SE owner
- Customer security/legal contact(s)

---

## Approval policy (who must sign off)
Any Security Appendix language that changes obligations must be approved by the functions below. Approval is based on the **final language** that will be sent to the customer.

### Approval matrix (minimum required)
- **Legal (required for all)**: Michael Grant or Sofia Mendes
- **Security Engineering (required when technical control commitments are created/changed)**: Marcus Lin
- **GRC/Compliance (required when compliance, audits, policies, SOC scope, or control attestations are referenced)**: Olga Petrov
- **Security & Compliance PM (required when changes impact enablement kit language alignment)**: Naomi Feldman

### Escalation
- High-risk commitments (e.g., audit rights, unlimited liability language embedded in appendix, fixed incident notification hours without qualifiers, broad warranties) must be escalated to:
  - **Dr. Aisha Rahman (CISO)** for security posture risk acceptance (as needed)
  - Finance/Legal leadership for commercial/legal risk acceptance (handled within Legal)

> Sales/SE note: Do not tell the customer that a clause is “approved” until Legal confirms approval in the ticket.

---

## Standard SLAs (what to expect)
These are targets, not guarantees; provide complete context to help us hit them.

- **Triage/acknowledgement:** 1 business day
- **Standard redline turnaround:** 5 business days
- **Complex / customer template addendum:** 7–10 business days
- **Expedite requests:** Case-by-case; must include close date and business justification

Common drivers of longer cycles:
- Missing source document/version
- Requests that require new technical validation (e.g., logging scope, retention behaviors)
- New compliance claims or audit commitments

---

## Redline tracking & storage (system of record)
### What we track
For every Security Appendix redline, we track:
- Customer, deal ID, and document version
- Summary of requested changes
- Legal position (accept / reject / propose alternate)
- Security/GRC approvals with dates
- Final customer-shared version and signature status

### Where documents live
- **System of record for negotiation:** Legal contracts repository (internal)
- **Working drafts:** Attached to the Legal intake ticket (preferred) or linked drive folder with restricted permissions
- **Final executed agreement:** Contract repository record + link in CRM (Sales/RevOps)

### Naming convention
Use consistent names to reduce confusion:
- `CustomerName_SecurityAppendix_Redwood-v<baseline>_CustomerRedlines_<YYYY-MM-DD>.docx`
- `CustomerName_SecurityAppendix_Redwood-v<baseline>_RedwoodResponse_<YYYY-MM-DD>.docx`
- `CustomerName_SecurityAppendix_Executed_<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf`

### What NOT to do
- Do not email redlines broadly (risk of outdated versions and access sprawl)
- Do not store customer security addenda in personal drives
- Do not copy/paste customer-proposed clauses into Slack without context (treat as confidential deal material)

---

## Step-by-step process
### Step 1 — Submit intake
Sales/SE submits Legal Intake with required information and attaches/redlines the document.

### Step 2 — Legal triage
Legal confirms:
- Correct baseline appendix and deal context
- Whether this is (a) standard negotiation, (b) security posture change, or (c) evidence request misrouted
- Whether Security Engineering and/or GRC review is required

Legal assigns a primary owner and sets target dates.

### Step 3 — Security/GRC review (as needed)
Security Engineering and/or GRC reviews clause changes and provides:
- Accept/reject guidance
- Approved alternate language (if available)
- Required qualifiers to avoid over-commitment (e.g., “as set forth in the Agreement”, “consistent with the Services purchased”, “subject to contract terms”)

### Step 4 — Consolidated redline response
Legal produces the consolidated response redline and posts it to the ticket with:
- Summary of material changes
- Open items requiring customer follow-up
- Approval log (who approved, date)

### Step 5 — Send to customer
Only Sales/SE (or Legal, depending on deal motion) sends the approved redline to customer.

### Step 6 — Closeout & archiving
Once agreed/executed:
- Final PDF is stored in the contract repository
- CRM (HubSpot/Salesforce) is updated with a link to the executed document and the final Security Appendix version
- Any new reusable language is submitted for inclusion in the **Standard RFP Response Library** / enablement kit (via Naomi Feldman)

---

## Guardrails: what we can and cannot commit to (high-level)
This section is not legal advice; it exists to reduce back-and-forth and avoid avoidable commitments.

Typically acceptable (with approved wording):
- Describing controls in line with Redwood’s published security enablement materials
- References to SOC 2 availability under NDA (without over-promising scope)
- Reasonable incident notification language that is consistent with the Agreement and avoids fixed “always within X hours” unless explicitly approved

Typically requires deeper review / often rejected:
- Customer audit rights that include on-site access to Redwood facilities without limitations
- Unlimited/custom breach notification timelines without qualifiers
- Commitments to provide customer-specific security artifacts not part of standard evidence set
- Commitments that imply product behavior not true across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (shared responsibility mismatch)

---

## Templates (internal)
### Intake subject line
`Security Appendix Redline – <Customer> – <Deal ID> – <Target Close Date>`

### Customer email (approved framing)
Use this framing to set expectations:
- We can review the requested changes and will respond with proposed language.
- Some security terms require internal review by Security/GRC and Legal.
- We will prioritize based on deal timeline and completeness of provided materials.

(For evidence requests, use the evidence sharing templates in the Customer Security Review Process page.)

---

## Ownership and maintenance
- **Process owner:** Finance/Legal (Contracts)
- **Security language owners:** Security & Compliance (Naomi Feldman) + GRC (Olga Petrov)
- **Technical control owners:** Security Engineering (Marcus Lin)

This page is reviewed quarterly or when any of the following change:
- New Security FAQ / enablement kit version
- Material product changes affecting security boundaries (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- Updated evidence sharing rules or NDA requirements

---

## FAQs
**Q: The customer wants a “quick confirmation” over email that we meet a requirement. Is that a Security Appendix change?**
A: If it is a contractual commitment or could be interpreted as one, treat it as a Security Appendix/legal request. Route via intake.

**Q: Can SEs propose alternate clause language directly?**
A: SEs can suggest language, but **Legal must send** the final approved redline, and Security/GRC must approve any new or modified security commitments.

**Q: Where do I find approved boilerplate for common security questions?**
A: Start with the **Standard RFP Response Library** and **Enterprise Security FAQ v2** (links above). If the customer needs it in contract form, open an intake request.
